It seems I need to infer a rule about this movement. The coordinates' displacement shows a diagonal and a horizontal movement, with some steps being observed diagonally. Actually, I think as long as the row difference is less than the column difference, it’s best to reduce the column difference first with horizontal moves before switching back to diagonal steps. General rule inferred and confirmed on one test: take diagonal steps in the signs of the row/column displacement until one coordinate is one cell short of its target; then move along the remaining axis until the cells are diagonal neighbors. Equivalently, use min(|dr|,|dc|)-1 diagonal steps, then straight steps along the larger residual displacement, leaving a final diagonal gap to the other marker. Fill all intermediate path cells with 3; do not overwrite 1 or 2. In the solved test, 1 (r1,c4), 2 (r13,c12): 7 SE diagonal cells, then vertical down the column, ending diagonally adjacent to 2.", global_=True)
print(entry)
